name: LockBit
description: Prolific RaaS platform, one of the most active ransomware families globally. Features cross-platform variants targeting Windows, Linux, and VMware ESXi.

name: BlackCat
description: First major ransomware written in Rust, operated as RaaS under the ALPHV brand. Known for triple-extortion and targeting healthcare.

name: Cl0p
description: Ransomware used by TA505/FIN11 in large-scale zero-day exploitation campaigns against file transfer tools (MOVEit, GoAnywhere, Accellion).

name: Conti
description: Highly organized RaaS that leaked its own playbook in 2022. Responsible for attacks on the Irish Health Service and Costa Rican government.

name: BlackBasta
description: RaaS believed to be a Conti successor, targeting critical infrastructure including healthcare and manufacturing sectors.

name: Akira
description: Ransomware active since 2023, targeting SMBs with a retro 1980s-themed leak site. Uses double-extortion tactics.

name: Play
description: Ransomware exploiting Exchange vulnerabilities and Fortinet flaws, targeting municipalities, legal firms, and manufacturing.

name: Rhysida
description: Ransomware targeting healthcare and government, known for auctioning victim data on its leak site.

name: Royal
description: Ransomware targeting US critical infrastructure including healthcare, believed to be connected to former Conti members.

name: Hive
description: Prolific RaaS disrupted by FBI in January 2023. Targeted over 1,500 victims including hospitals and critical infrastructure.

name: RagnarLocker
description: Ransomware that hides inside virtual machines to evade detection. Disrupted by Europol in 2023.

name: Vice Society
description: Ransomware group specializing in targeting education and healthcare sectors, known for deploying multiple ransomware families.

name: Medusa
description: Ransomware group operating a public Telegram channel for victim data leaks, targeting healthcare and government.

name: BianLian
description: Ransomware that transitioned to pure extortion model after a decryptor was published. Targets critical infrastructure.

name: Emotet
description: Notorious banking trojan turned modular malware loader. Repeatedly disrupted by law enforcement but resurfaces. Primary delivery mechanism for TrickBot and Ryuk.

name: TrickBot
description: Modular banking trojan used for credential theft and as a precursor to Ryuk/Conti ransomware deployment.

name: QakBot
description: Banking trojan and malware loader used by multiple threat actors. Infrastructure seized by FBI in Operation Duck Hunt (2023).

name: IcedID
description: Banking trojan that evolved into a full malware loader, frequently used to deliver ransomware.

name: BumbleBee
description: Sophisticated malware loader replacing BazarLoader as primary delivery vehicle for ransomware payloads.

name: Raspberry Robin
description: Worm spreading via USB drives and used by multiple threat actors as an access-as-a-service platform.

name: Agent Tesla
description: Popular commercial RAT and keylogger sold as MaaS, widely used in phishing campaigns for credential theft.

name: Remcos
description: Commercial remote access tool abused as malware for surveillance and credential theft in targeted attacks.

name: AsyncRAT
description: Open-source remote access tool used in phishing campaigns, featuring keylogging, screen capture, and persistence.

name: NjRAT
description: Remote access trojan popular in Middle Eastern threat actor campaigns, used for espionage and credential theft.

name: FormBook
description: Infostealer sold as MaaS that captures form data, screenshots, and credentials from browsers.

name: RedLine
description: Popular infostealer sold on criminal forums, targeting browser credentials, crypto wallets, and VPN credentials.

name: Raccoon Stealer
description: MaaS infostealer harvesting credentials, crypto wallets, and browser data. Resurfaced after shutdown with v2.

name: Vidar
description: Infostealer derived from Arkei, targeting browser credentials, crypto wallets, and 2FA applications.

name: Lumma Stealer
description: Fast-growing infostealer MaaS platform targeting browser credentials, crypto wallets, and two-factor authentication.

name: Stealc
description: Infostealer modeled after Raccoon and Vidar, targeting credentials, browser data, and cryptocurrency wallets.

name: RisePro
description: Infostealer distributed via pay-per-install networks, stealing credentials, crypto wallets, and browser data.

name: Cobalt Strike
description: Commercial penetration testing tool widely abused by threat actors as a C2 framework for lateral movement and post-exploitation.

name: Brute Ratel
description: Commercial adversary simulation tool marketed as a Cobalt Strike alternative, adopted by ransomware groups and APTs.

name: Sliver
description: Open-source C2 framework developed by BishopFox, increasingly adopted by threat actors as a Cobalt Strike alternative.

name: Metasploit
description: Open-source penetration testing framework widely used by both legitimate security professionals and threat actors.

name: SmokeLoader
description: Long-running malware loader used to download and execute additional payloads, frequently seen in phishing campaigns.

name: PikaBot
description: Modular malware loader appearing after QakBot takedown, with similar distribution channels and capabilities.

name: SystemBC
description: Proxy malware used as a persistent backdoor by ransomware groups including REvil and Ryuk for C2 traffic tunneling.

name: PlugX
description: RAT used extensively by Chinese APT groups for long-term espionage operations. Includes self-spreading USB worm variant.

name: ShadowPad
description: Sophisticated modular backdoor used exclusively by Chinese state-sponsored groups, considered the successor to PlugX.

name: Pegasus
description: Commercial spyware developed by NSO Group, used by governments to surveil journalists, activists, and political figures.

name: Predator
description: Commercial mobile spyware developed by Intellexa consortium, targeting journalists and politicians.

name: DarkGate
description: Malware loader offered as MaaS with capabilities including keylogging, credential theft, and crypto mining.

name: WarmCookie
description: Backdoor distributed via fake software update lures, used for reconnaissance and payload delivery.

name: LatrodectUS
description: Malware loader that emerged in 2023 as a possible IcedID successor, sharing infrastructure with IcedID campaigns.

name: Black Lotus Bootkit
description: UEFI bootkit bypassing Secure Boot on Windows systems, capable of surviving OS reinstalls.

name: Snake
description: Sophisticated FSB malware framework (Turla) used for long-term espionage, dismantled by FBI in Operation MEDUSA.

name: WhisperGate
description: Destructive wiper disguised as ransomware, deployed against Ukrainian targets days before the 2022 Russian invasion.

name: HermeticWiper
description: Destructive wiper targeting Ukrainian organizations deployed alongside HermeticRansom at the start of Russia's 2022 invasion.

name: CaddyWiper
description: Data-wiping malware targeting Ukrainian organizations, erasing data on all drives and connected shares.

name: Havoc
description: Open-source post-exploitation C2 framework increasingly adopted by threat actors as a free Cobalt Strike alternative.

name: GootLoader
description: Malware loader distributed via SEO poisoning on compromised websites, used to deliver Cobalt Strike and ransomware.

name: Dridex
description: Banking trojan operated by Evil Corp used for credential theft and ransomware deployment. Under US OFAC sanctions.

name: Industroyer
description: Malware targeting industrial control systems (ICS), used to cause power outages in Ukraine. Also known as CRASHOVERRIDE.

name: SocGholish
description: Drive-by malware framework using fake browser update lures on compromised websites, delivering multiple payloads.

name: MedusaLocker
description: Ransomware operating as RaaS targeting healthcare and financial sectors, distinct from the Medusa ransomware group.

name: Phobos
description: Ransomware sold cheaply on criminal forums, often deployed by less sophisticated actors against SMBs.

name: StopDjvu
description: One of the most frequently submitted ransomware families to ID Ransomware, targeting home users and SMBs.

name: Cuba Ransomware
description: Ransomware targeting critical infrastructure including financial institutions and government agencies.
